function: RIS phase-shift optimization (binary phase states) to maximize individual-user RSSI or the minimum RSSI across users, using only RSSI feedback and no CSI (p. 2).
system: M=4-antenna WiFi AP (TP-Link Archer AX20), U=2 single-antenna UEs, two concatenated Greenerwave 1-bit reflecting RIS (N=152), 5.24 GHz, 20 MHz (p. 4).
method: CEMAB: cross-entropy multi-armed bandit, a lightweight reinforcement-learning method with importance sampling; no neural network; online learning from RSSI reward on the testbed (p. 2-3).
data_channel: Measured RSSI from a real indoor WiFi testbed, AP about 2 m away in line of sight, fixed quasi-static environment; no channel model or dataset (p. 4).
test_conditions: Same fixed environment and user locations for all runs; two objectives (per-user RSSI, max-min RSSI); up to T=10 iterations, K=100 samples, averaged over 100 collections (p. 4-5).
baselines: Learned: conventional epsilon-greedy MAB [7]; non-learned: random RIS configurations (average of 100), no RIS (p. 4).
metrics: RSSI in dBm of the target user and minimum RSSI across users, versus number of iterations; gains in dB over baselines (p. 4-5).
complexity: Computational complexity approximately O(TKN) (T iterations, K samples, N elements); convergence within eight iterations; no runtime or FLOPs reported (p. 3, 5).
q1_support: p. 4: "All experiments are performed using WiFi communications in an indoor environment."; p. 2: "experimentally using a real-world WiFi-based testbed"; the RSSI is measured live on hardware, so the data are measured, not simulated.
q2_support: p. 4: "Throughout the experiments, the environment and user locations are kept fixed"; p. 5: "Future work will extend this approach to more dynamic environments"; both case studies share one setup and the algorithm is rerun for each objective.
q3_support: p. 4: "MAB [7]: This method is the conventional ϵ-greedy MAB algorithm" (earlier learned method); p. 4: "Random: The performance is given by the average RSSI over 100 random RIS configurations." (non-learned); both compared on RSSI in Figs. 3 and 4.
q4_support: p. 3: "The overall computational complexity of the proposed CEMAB algorithm is approximately O(TKN)".
q5_support: p. 2: "Real-world experimental validation is conducted through two case studies"; all results are measured on the authors' WiFi testbed (p. 4). Met only through the measured-data clause: the paper gives no link to code or data.
notes: Included although the learner is a lightweight bandit with no neural network: the paper frames CEMAB as a reinforcement learning algorithm that learns per-element mean rewards and a sampling distribution from RSSI feedback (p. 1-3). Area 3 (RIS phase shifts). q1 and q5 are met through the measured-data clause, since every result is a live RSSI measurement on a physical testbed. q3 caveat: the MAB benchmark [7] is an earlier published learned method, but it is also CEMAB without importance sampling; if the reviewer reads it as an ablation, q3 becomes 0. Title and DOI 10.1109/LCOMM.2025.3614755 are on p. 1.
